defects: The 9.1s middle shot is one action repeated eight times: a breaker flips and a name lights. The spacing between flips is the same each time, with no build in tempo or scale.
In the vertical SUBSTATION entrance, ghosted names sit behind the wordmark and collide with it (frame 2). The overlap reads as muddy layering, not a designed reveal.
The peak flash washes the whole frame to beige at low contrast. Names and the wordmark become nearly unreadable, so the peak frame is weak.
The opening 50 Hz waveform is static and sparse for about 2s, the strongest dead air in the piece. The flat noise riser under it does not resolve into the next shot.
The ending only adds the date and the TICKETS FRIDAY block to the panel already on screen. There is no new move, and nothing calls back to the waveform opening.

Small details are slightly soft. The red F01–F08 labels and the monospace tagline are thin and low contrast at 100%, and a stray light rectangle on the bus bar near F04 looks like a leftover artifact.
gaps: Motion has no weight or variety. The switches snap linearly with no overshoot or settle, the camera never moves, nothing moves in depth, and the eight closures do not speed up. A top studio would compress the sequence, cascade the last switches together and let the system visibly power up: current running along the bus, light spilling outward, the frame shaking.

The sound sits in a sparse middle. One identical, pitch-swept click sample repeats eight times with silence between, framed by a noise riser at the start and a dense loop at the end. There is no low-end build, hum or electrical sound design that grows as each circuit closes.

Transitions and the overall structure are weak. The wave-to-wordmark cut and the white flash are blunt hard switches. The idea (a lineup shown as feeders closing on a breaker panel) is good, but it stays a single lock-off with no shot change, and it lacks a payoff that returns to the 50 Hz wave.
